drafts.text:
HOOK
Major US growth data is dropping today, and active traders need to be ready.
[ON SCREEN: Tiger to camera, graphic headline US Q3 GDP]

WHAT IT IS
At 08:30 ET, the second estimate for US Q3 GDP hits the tape. Markets are looking for 3.5%, following 2.2% in the initial reading.
[ON SCREEN: Forecast 3.5% vs Previous 2.2%]

WHY IT MATTERS
This release provides a crucial health check on the world's largest economy. That momentum directly drives the US Dollar Index, EUR/USD, and broad equity markets like the S&P 500.
[ON SCREEN: US Dollar Index, EUR/USD, S&P 500 tickers]

WHAT TO WATCH
A print coming in above 3.5% could lift the greenback as traders scale back rate cut bets. On the flip side, a surprise drop below forecast could pressure the dollar, giving EUR/USD room to rally while stocks reassess growth risks.
[ON SCREEN: Bullish Dollar vs Bearish Dollar scenarios]

drafts.text:
HOOK
Is German consumer sentiment finally turning the corner ahead of the new month?
[ON SCREEN: Germany GfK Consumer Confidence / EUR/USD]

WHAT IT IS
Germany releases its GfK Consumer Confidence survey for Dec at 02:00 ET. Markets are looking for a print of -28.5, compared to -30.8 in the prior reading.
[ON SCREEN: Forecast -28.5 vs Previous -30.8]

WHY IT MATTERS
Germany is the powerhouse of the eurozone. When German households feel cautious, consumer spending slows. Currency traders follow this closely because consumer sentiment can weigh on economic growth and steer pairs like EUR/USD.
[ON SCREEN: EUR/USD Chart]

WHAT TO WATCH
A result coming in better than -28.5 could give EUR/USD a lift early in the session. But if the data misses, traders will watch for renewed pressure on the euro.
[ON SCREEN: Scenarios: Above -28.5 vs Below -28.5]
